document_text:
# Kaffeekontor Nord – Company and Product Brief

Launch of Nordbrew Oat Cold Brew in Germany. Internal document for the launch planning team. All companies, people and figures in this document are fictional and used for evaluation only.

## 1. Company overview

Kaffeekontor Nord ApS is a Danish coffee roaster founded in 2017 in Aarhus by Signe Holm, a former barista champion, and Jonas Lund, previously a sales manager at a Danish dairy cooperative. The company roasts specialty coffee and sells it to cafés, offices and consumers.

In 2024 the company had 41 employees and a turnover of 9.6 million euros: 70% in Denmark, 30% in Sweden. Its products are sold in about 1,800 points of sale (supermarkets, convenience stores and cafés) and through its own online shop, which accounts for 12% of sales. The company raised 6 million euros in 2025 to launch its ready-to-drink range in Germany.

## 2. The product: Nordbrew Oat Cold Brew

Nordbrew is a cold brew coffee with oat drink, sold chilled in 250 ml cans. It was launched in Denmark in 2023 and now accounts for 38% of company turnover.

- Cold brewed for 18 hours from single-origin Arabica (Colombia and Ethiopia).
- 110 mg of caffeine per can, 2.1 g of sugar per 100 ml (no added sugar).
- Two variants: Original and Vanilla. An Espresso Strong variant is planned for 2026.
- Vegan, lactose-free, organic certified (EU organic label).
- Shelf life of 6 months refrigerated; it needs a chilled shelf.
- Recyclable aluminium can, with the German deposit (Pfand) of 0.25 euros.

In a Danish taste test run by the company in 2024 (300 participants), 52% preferred Nordbrew to the leading canned iced coffee with milk, 18% had no preference and 30% preferred the competitor. Participants liked the low sweetness; 22% found the Original variant too bitter.

Intended shelf price in Germany: 2.49 euros per can (deposit excluded).

## 3. Why Germany, and launch goals

Germany is the largest ready-to-drink (RTD) coffee market in Europe, and oat drinks are the fastest growing plant-based drink category there.

Goals for the German launch, approved by the board in May 2025:

- Reach a 3% value share of the German chilled RTD coffee category within 24 months.
- Be listed in at least 3,500 points of sale in the first year.
- Generate 30% of company turnover from Germany by the end of 2027.

The launch is planned for April 2026, starting with Hamburg, Berlin and the Rhine-Ruhr region.

## 4. Market context

Figures from the report "Chilled coffee drinks in Germany 2025" by BevData Research and from the Deutsches Getränkepanel 2025 consumer survey (both fictional sources for this evaluation).

| Indicator | Value | Source |
|---|---|---|
| Chilled RTD coffee category in Germany (2024) | 610 million euros | BevData Research 2025 |
| Category growth 2021-2024 | +7% per year | BevData Research 2025 |
| Plant-based share of the category | 14% | BevData Research 2025 |
| Adults who bought chilled RTD coffee in the last 3 months | 23% | Getränkepanel 2025 |

Sales by channel (2024): supermarkets and discounters 54%, petrol stations and convenience stores 24%, train-station and airport kiosks 13%, online and other 9%.

## 5. Consumer groups

The Getränkepanel 2025 measured interest in "a canned cold brew coffee with oat drink, low sugar, at about 2.50 euros" among German adults aged 18 to 64 (about 52 million people).

| Group | Adults | Share of adults 18-64 | Purchase intent |
|---|---|---|---|
| Specialty coffee enthusiasts (home baristas, specialty café regulars) | 0.5 million | 1% | 76% |
| Commuters who buy coffee on the go at least weekly | 11.4 million | 22% | 34% |
| Students | 2.6 million | 5% | 41% |
| Office workers who drink coffee at their desk | 8.9 million | 17% | 27% |

Specialty coffee enthusiasts are by far the most interested group, and they make up 81% of Nordbrew's Instagram community in Denmark. They mostly buy in specialty cafés and online. Commuters mostly buy at petrol stations, kiosks and supermarkets near transport hubs.

## 6. Competitors

- **Emmi Caffè Latte**: the category leader, sold in most supermarkets and petrol stations; milk-based, sweetened.
- **Starbucks chilled cups (Arla)**: strong brand, wide distribution, sweetened milk coffee.
- **Oatly Iced Coffee**: oat-based, smaller distribution, mainly organic shops and supermarkets in large cities.
- **Private labels** of the large discounters: lower prices, entered the category in 2022.

No price comparison has been carried out yet.

## 7. Distribution and marketing

Kaffeekontor Nord is negotiating with one national beverage wholesaler, which supplies supermarkets and petrol stations. A pilot with a train-station kiosk chain (about 400 kiosks) is under discussion. The online shop will ship to Germany from launch.

The marketing budget for the first year is 1.2 million euros.

## 8. Open points

- Target group: the founders lean towards specialty coffee enthusiasts, because they love the product and are active on social media. The sales team prefers commuters. No decision yet.
- Positioning for Germany.
- Launch campaign concept and channel plan.
- Whether to launch the Vanilla variant at the same time as Original.

analysis.market_overview: The German chilled RTD coffee category was worth 610 million euros in 2024 and grew about 7% per year from 2021 to 2024; plant-based products hold 14% of it [S3]. 23% of adults bought chilled RTD coffee in the last 3 months [S3]. By channel, supermarkets and discounters account for 54% of sales, petrol stations and convenience stores 24%, train-station and airport kiosks 13%, and online and other 9% [S3]. The document calls Germany Europe's largest RTD coffee market and oat drinks its fastest-growing plant-based drink category [S2]. The 3% value share goal equals about 18.3 million euros, derived from the 2024 category size [S2, S3]. Web research found few German prices. The only German chilled RTD price point is Emmi Caffè Latte Macchiato at 2.99 euros per 230 ml cup [S6]. Nordbrew's planned 2.49 euros per 250 ml can (deposit excluded) is below that. All market figures come from the document; no independent web source confirms them.

competitors.name: Emmi Caffè Latte
competitors.positioning: Category leader, sold in most supermarkets and petrol stations; milk-based and sweetened, in a recyclable cup [S5]. One German retailer lists the Macchiato 230 ml at 2.99 euros (13.00 euros per litre), with multi-buy discounts down to 2.70 euros [S6]. An Austrian retailer lists it at 1.99 euros [S7], so prices vary a lot by retailer.

competitors.name: Starbucks chilled cups (Arla)
competitors.positioning: Strong brand with wide distribution and sweetened milk coffee [S5]. Starbucks Caffè Latte Eiskaffee 220 ml is listed in REWE's online shop; no price was visible [S8].

competitors.name: Oatly Iced Coffee
competitors.positioning: Oat-based; per the document it has smaller distribution, mainly organic shops and supermarkets in large cities [S5]. Oatly's German site lists Barista Iced Flat White and Iced Cappuccino in 235 ml cartocans, but the Flat White page says it is only available in Switzerland [S9]. German availability is unconfirmed.

competitors.name: Private labels of the large discounters
competitors.positioning: Lower-priced own brands that entered the category in 2022 [S5]. One example is Aldi Nord's Moreno 'Typ Eiskaffee mit Milch', 275 g can, at 1.59 euros. It looks ambient rather than chilled, so it is a weak comparison [S10].

competitors.name: Coffrigo Oat Milk Latte
competitors.positioning: Direct concept match: nitro cold brew coffee (70%) with oat drink, vegan, no added sugar. Sold direct-to-consumer and in 24-packs via honest-rare.de [S11, S12]. Retail reach is unknown.

competitors.name: Mövenpick Cold Brew Coffee
competitors.positioning: Described as the first brand in Germany to offer ready-to-drink cold brew on the chilled shelf, as a lifestyle drink [S13]. The page is undated.

customer_needs: Low sweetness: participants in the Danish taste test liked Nordbrew's low sweetness [S1]
Low sugar: the German consumer survey tested a low-sugar canned cold brew with oat drink, and competitors such as Emmi and Starbucks are sweetened [S4, S5]
Less bitterness: 22% of Danish taste-test participants found the Original variant too bitter [S1]
Plant-based options: plant-based products already hold 14% of the category [S3], and oat drinks are the fastest-growing plant-based drink category in Germany [S2]
Oat-based coffee without added sugar: Coffrigo positions itself on this [S11]
Convenient on-the-go purchase near transport hubs, petrol stations, kiosks and supermarkets (commuters) [S4]
Specialty coffee enthusiasts mostly buy in specialty cafés and online [S4]
A price around 2.50 euros: the survey measured interest at about that price [S4]
Lower prices: discounter private labels compete on price [S5]

data_quality_notes: Market size, growth, plant-based share, channel split and consumer-group figures come only from the company document, which cites BevData Research 2025 and Getränkepanel 2025. The document says both are fictional. No independent web source confirms them.

The research found no German shelf prices for Starbucks, Oatly, Coffrigo, Mövenpick or a chilled discounter private label. Price level is therefore 'unknown' for most competitors, and the document's own price comparison has not been carried out.

The only German chilled RTD price is Emmi at 2.99 euros per 230 ml cup at one retailer (combi.de), which is a single data point. The Austrian Billa price of 1.99 euros is not German and shows wide retailer variation. Nordbrew at 2.49 euros per 250 ml (9.96 euros per litre) looks below Emmi's 13.00 euros per litre on this basis. With the 0.25 euro deposit the consumer pays 2.74 euros (my arithmetic from the brief).

The private-label price (Aldi Nord Moreno 1.59 euros, 275 g) is a weak comparison. It looks like an ambient, possibly instant-coffee-type product rather than a chilled RTD coffee. I classed private labels as 'low' mainly on the document's statement that they have lower prices.

Conflict on Oatly: the document says Oatly Iced Coffee is sold in German organic shops and city supermarkets. Oatly's German site lists 235 ml cartocans, and the Flat White page says it is only available in Switzerland. I could not confirm German availability; it needs verification.
The Mövenpick page is undated and may be old. Coffrigo's retail reach is unknown. A Berlin sweetened cold brew seen in the research is not a clear brand and was left out of the competitor list.

The taste-test evidence is Danish, run by the company (300 participants) and against one unnamed competitor. It is not German evidence. 52% preferred Nordbrew, 18% had no preference and 30% preferred the competitor [S1].

Segment sizes come from the document. It does not say whether the groups overlap, so I did not add them together. The intent-weighted figures in the research log are my arithmetic, not source figures, and I did not use them as sizes.
Specialty enthusiasts have the highest intent (76%) but are the smallest group (0.5M). The Instagram share (81%) is a Danish community figure and does not measure the German market.
No external German evidence was found on any segment or on consumer needs. Needs come from the document and a few web product pages, so they are partly inferred from competitor positioning.
The 3% value share goal (about 18.3M euros) uses the 2024 category size and ignores growth since then. This is my derivation.

strategy.target_description: Commuters in Germany: adults who buy coffee on the go at least weekly. They mostly buy at petrol stations, kiosks and supermarkets near transport hubs.
strategy.positioning_statement: For German commuters who want a cold coffee on the go without the sugar, Nordbrew Oat Cold Brew is the chilled, organic, plant-based cold brew in a can. It is cold brewed for 18 hours from single-origin Arabica, with no added sugar (2.1 g per 100 ml). Unlike the sweetened milk-based leaders Emmi and Starbucks, it offers a lighter, lower-sugar and vegan alternative. Unlike niche oat players such as Coffrigo, it aims to be on the shelf where commuters already shop.
strategy.value_proposition: A genuine cold brew with oat drink that is easy to pick up on the way: no added sugar, vegan and organic, in a 250 ml can at a price near the 2.50 euro level commuters were tested on.
strategy.pricing_direction: Keep 2.49 euros (deposit excluded; 2.74 euros with the 0.25 euro Pfand, my arithmetic) as a provisional price, and do not go above it. The only German chilled price point is Emmi Caffè Latte Macchiato at 2.99 euros per 230 ml at one retailer, with multi-buy offers down to 2.70 euros [S6]. Nordbrew sits slightly below it per can. Prices for Starbucks, Oatly, Coffrigo and Mövenpick are unknown, and private labels are described as lower-priced [S5]. Do not try to match the discounters. Before listing negotiations, run the planned shelf-price check across German retailers and kiosks and confirm 2.49 euros. Hold it if comparable cold brews sell at similar levels. Lower it only if the check shows that commuters' reference prices are clearly lower.
strategy.rationale: Commuters are the best fit once size, interest and accessibility are read together. Size: SEG2 has 11.4M adults (22% of adults 18-64), against 0.5M enthusiasts (1%), 2.6M students (5%) and 8.9M office workers (17%) [S4]. Interest: the enthusiasts have the highest purchase intent (76%), but at 0.5M they are too small for the goals. The 3% value share is about 18.3M euros [S2, S3], and 3,500 points of sale need mass retail. Commuter intent is 34%, ahead of office workers (27%) and below students (41%) [S4]. As an illustration only (my arithmetic, not source figures, and intent definitions may differ between groups), intent times size gives roughly 0.4M for enthusiasts, 3.9M for commuters, 1.1M for students and 2.4M for office workers. Commuters therefore have the largest pool of likely buyers. Accessibility: the enthusiasts buy mainly in specialty cafés and online [S4]. Online and other channels are only 9% of category sales [S3], and the company's online shop is only 12% of its sales. Commuters buy where the category sells: petrol stations and convenience stores 24%, train-station and airport kiosks 13%, supermarkets and discounters 54% [S3]. This matches the company's ongoing wholesaler talks and the possible kiosk pilot of about 400 kiosks. Competition: Emmi and Starbucks are widely available but sweetened, milk-based [S5]. A low-sugar, plant-based can is a clear difference, and plant-based products already hold 14% of a category worth 610M euros that grew about 7% a year [S3]. Coffrigo is a direct concept match (oat, cold brew, no added sugar), but its retail reach is unknown [S11]. Claims used: no added sugar, vegan, organic, 18-hour single-origin cold brew, all from the product description. I deliberately avoid the "52% preferred Nordbrew" taste-test claim because it is Danish, company-run and against one unnamed competitor [S1]. I also avoid a "less bitter" claim, since 22% of testers found the Original too bitter [S1]. Assumptions and risks: all market and segment figures come from one company document that the analysis notes as unverified by independent sources. The kiosk pilot and the wholesaler deal are not confirmed, so the supermarket listings carry the 3,500-point goal. Discounters, which are part of the 54% supermarket and discounter channel, are not targeted because private labels compete on price there. The Vanilla variant could suit commuters who find Original bitter, but that is my assumption and needs testing in Germany. Specialty enthusiasts can be a secondary audience, through social media, to build credibility, but not the main target. Oatly's German availability is unconfirmed, so I do not rely on it as a competitor in the positioning.

campaign.concept: "Der Weg ist dein Moment": the daily commute becomes a small pause with a can of cold brew that has nothing to hide. Every execution shows the journey in short, real moments (platform, petrol station, tram) and ends on the can and its simple facts: 18 hours cold brewed, no added sugar, vegan, organic. The idea expresses the positioning by making Nordbrew the chilled, plant-based cold coffee that is simply there on the way, where commuters already shop.
campaign.tagline: Cold Brew für unterwegs. Ohne Zuckerzusatz.

key_messages.body: Nordbrew Oat Cold Brew: 18 Stunden kalt gebrüht, mit Hafer-Drink, ohne Zuckerzusatz (2,1 g pro 100 ml). Vegan, bio, in der handlichen 250-ml-Dose. Jetzt im Kühlregal an der Kasse.

key_messages.headline: Dein Zug kommt. Dein Cold Brew steht schon bereit.
key_messages.body: Greif zu, bevor die Türen schließen: Nordbrew Oat Cold Brew, 250 ml, eiskalt aus dem Kiosk-Kühlregal. Ohne Zuckerzusatz, vegan und bio. 2,49 € zzgl. 0,25 € Pfand.

key_messages.headline: Cold Brew aus Aarhus. Jetzt im Kühlregal.
key_messages.body: Sorte: Single-Origin-Arabica aus Kolumbien und Äthiopien, 18 Stunden kalt gebrüht und mit Hafer-Drink abgerundet. Ohne Zuckerzusatz, vegan, bio-zertifiziert. Die 250-ml-Dose findest du im Kühlregal.

key_messages.headline: 18 Stunden Cold Brew. 0 g Zuckerzusatz.
key_messages.body: Nordbrew Oat Cold Brew. Vegan, bio, ohne Zuckerzusatz. Jetzt am Bahnhof und an der Tankstelle.

key_messages.headline: Dein Weg zur Arbeit hat ein Upgrade verdient.
key_messages.body: Bahnsteig, Dose auf, ein kalter Schluck. Nordbrew Oat Cold Brew: 18 Stunden kalt gebrüht, ohne Zuckerzusatz, vegan und bio. Zeig uns deinen Pendelmoment mit #MeinNordbrewMoment.

content_ideas: Cold-storage cooler branding and shelf-strip wobblers for petrol stations and convenience stores, with the line 'Kalt gestellt. Schnell gegriffen.' and a simple fact panel (18 h cold brew, no added sugar, vegan, organic).
Branded chilled display units and counter stickers in train-station kiosks, designed for a 5-second grab-and-go purchase, if the kiosk pilot is confirmed.
Transit out-of-home campaign in station posters, platform screens and tram/S-Bahn interiors in major German commuter cities, with large can visual and the facts '18 h cold brewed, 0 g added sugar'.
Series of 15-second vertical videos showing commute moments (platform, bike, tram) ending with the can opening sound and the tagline.
User-generated video challenge #MeinNordbrewMoment inviting commuters to share their daily commute pause, with reposts on the brand account.
Short 'How it's made' video clips: 18-hour cold brew, Colombian and Ethiopian single-origin Arabica, from Aarhus roastery, told in 20 seconds.
Supermarket chilled-shelf navigation: shelf-edge strips and secondary placement near transport-hub stores, with clear 'no added sugar, vegan, organic' call-outs.
Launch sampling of chilled cans at selected busy station entrances during morning rush hour in launch month.
campaign.visual_direction: Clean Nordic style: lots of white space, cool and calm. Palette of deep cold-brew brown and off-white, with a fresh glacier-blue accent for the 'cold' cue and a small organic-green touch for the EU organic label. Imagery: real commute scenes in soft morning light (platforms, tram windows, petrol station coolers), condensation on a chilled aluminium can held in one hand, close-ups of the can opening. Typography: bold, simple sans-serif with short headlines legible in 2 seconds from a moving train. Packaging cues: matte aluminium can with a clear large 'Oat Cold Brew' name, icon row for 'no added sugar', vegan and organic, and the EU organic logo; the key facts always readable on the front. Photography and video should be natural and unhurried, with no gym or performance imagery.

issues.message: S5 is the company document, section 6. It describes Emmi Caffè Latte as the category leader, sold in most supermarkets and petrol stations, milk-based and sweetened. It says nothing about a recyclable cup. The packaging claim has no cited support. Remove it, or cite a source that states it, such as the Emmi product page. Evidence: analysis.competitors[0].positioning = "milk-based and sweetened, in a recyclable cup [S5]"

The value proposition rests on no added sugar, vegan, oat and cold brew. The analysis shows Coffrigo already offers this (nitro cold brew with oat drink, vegan, no added sugar). Oatly is also oat-based. The only difference from Coffrigo in the positioning is shelf presence, and that depends on a wholesaler deal and a kiosk pilot that are not confirmed. Add a product-level differentiator that Coffrigo does not claim, such as the EU organic label, the 18-hour single-origin process or the can format. Otherwise state openly that distribution is the main difference. Evidence: strategy.value_proposition = "A genuine cold brew with oat drink that is easy to pick up on the way: no added sugar, vegan and organic"

The copy states 2.49 € as a firm shelf price. The strategy calls it provisional, pending a German shelf-price check, and the brief says no competitor price comparison has been done. Take the price out of the copy until it is confirmed. Retailers also set shelf prices themselves, so the copy should not fix one. Evidence: campaign.key_messages[1].body = "2,49 € zzgl. 0,25 € Pfand."

This announces availability at stations and petrol stations as a fact. The wholesaler deal is still being negotiated and the kiosk pilot of about 400 kiosks is only under discussion. The same applies to 'Jetzt im Kühlregal an der Kasse' in the petrol-station message and to the kiosk message. Word these in the future tense or make them conditional on the listings. Evidence: campaign.key_messages[3].body = "Jetzt am Bahnhof und an der Tankstelle."

The supermarket message leads on origin and bean provenance (Aarhus, Colombia and Ethiopia, 'Sorte: Single-Origin-Arabica'). That is a specialty-enthusiast argument. The commuter need is convenience and a grab-and-go purchase near transport hubs. Reuse the commute angle and the short 'no added sugar' facts, as in the other messages. The body also starts with an awkward 'Sorte:' label. Evidence: campaign.key_messages[2].body = "Cold Brew aus Aarhus. Jetzt im Kühlregal."
